evidence: enumeration-contract.v1.md:164 requires inventories as well as plan/plan_id; :111-121 requires one actual inventory outcome per expected cell/program/kind.
IE:1464-1470 distinguishes pre-execution selected locators from provider-attributed symbol declarations and examined paths.

PROPOSAL.md:726-728 selects imports-cell symbol inventories, so an empty inventory list cannot satisfy this call for an ordinary available program.

Run full inventory admission after inventories have been produced/admitted and before evaluation, then through Run closure/replay, preserving input-origin fault routing. requiredFindings.problem: The session starts after X2 admission, but X2 has already read the project marker that the proposed walk later inventories; there is no exact capture handoff or operational-read boundary covering this path.
evidence: At 30c5db1, project_admission.rs:872 invokes observe_marker; :604 reads .opensip/project-id.v1; :536-545 and :612-615 retain decoded project ID/metadata rather than a raw C1 capture.
PROPOSAL.md:75 says the session opens after X2 and before the first project-file read, while :72 and :94 require one read and one project-file read site.
PROPOSAL.md:891 expressly inventories project-id.v1 because .opensip is not currently pruned.
project_admission.rs:797,818 re-observe the marker through byte reads; these mandatory operational checks need a precise boundary with the source-read prohibition.
requiredFindings.fix: Define an exact retained X2 marker-capture handoff into C1 for an inventoried marker, or choose and successor-gate a lawful discovery disposition for operational marker bytes. Specify the relation to X2 owner rechecks and preserve root/tracking admission prerequisites. Name and gate X2/B/C interface changes; extend the one-read/mutation controls to an already registered project with a present marker.

requiredFindings.problem: The archive profile charges physical tar framing and long-name headers against protocol counters whose quantities are logical dependency files and their content bytes, then labels exhaustion a whole-set bound breach.
evidence: NE:2876-2878 defines file manifest entries/data seal totals; NE:1663-1664 and NEM:1874 define fileCount and totalBytes from logical file contents; NE:2931-2932 fixes their entry/byte limits.
An in-profile long-path file has an L header plus its regular header. 500001 such files produce 1000002 physical entry headers while staying below the 1000000 logical-file bound.
A source set exactly at the 8 GiB logical-content bound has additional tar headers, padding, long-name data and end blocks, so physical decompressed bytes exceed its logical-byte allowance.
arithmetic_checks.json contains counter arithmetic only; no archives were constructed or decoded.
requiredFindings.fix: Use exact protocol counters for regular logical files/content bytes. Define separate archive-processing counters and explicit bounds/dispositions for inflated bytes, metadata/header work, padding/end scanning and compressed-input work. Derive the two-header allowance from the file cap or declare an independent stricter decoder limit. Add boundary controls distinguishing framing from content and control records from files.
